messages:
Alex: Heads up — saw a 2x spike in us-west GPU queue at 03:20 UTC, autoscaler started oscillating and we hit admission soft-shed twice. p95 token latency spiked to ~2.1s.

Maria: OK can you paste metrics? which shard? :thinking:

Alex: us-west-gpu-3 primarily. queue_depth ~480 -> 1200 over 6m. autoscale created 4 nodes then removed 3 quickly. logs show prewarm not finishing.

Devon: Classic warmup lag + scale-down hysteresis. We need smoother headroom and a way to avoid rejecting traffic from canary customers.

Alex: Proposal: adaptive credit allocator — give each shard a "ingress credit" budget computed from recent successful accepts and expected warmup rate. Low-priority classes get a token cost multiplier so they get shed first.

Sam: sounds good. quick sketch config:

```
admission:
  credit_window_sec: 60
  base_credits_per_shard: 1000
  warmup_rate_limit: 50/s
  priority_multipliers:
    realtime: 1.0
    background: 2.5
    internal: 5.0
```

Devon: Also add slow-rolloff for credits (exponential decay) to prevent step-changes during short bursts.

Maria: How do we measure success? key metrics: queue_depth, accept_rate_by_priority, p95_gen_latency, nodes_added_per_min, cost_delta. We should run a canary in us-west with 5% of traffic.

Alex: Plan: implement allocator + ingress shed middleware that drops requests when credits exhausted, with 429 and Retry-After header. Canary for 72h. Rollback if error rate for 'realtime' > 1%.

Sam: Also add trace id header and special metric labels: admission.credit_used, admission.shed_count, admission.retry_after_ms

Devon: + add an emergency bypass toggle per-customer for enterprise tiers.

Maria: I'll create the RFC and tracking doc. Action items: Alex implement POC, Sam add metrics, Devon add config flags. Sync tomorrow 10:00 PT.

ingest-bot: Deploy canary scheduled: us-west 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC :white_check_mark:

Alex: cool, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
